answer: One concrete defence is a stake-backed vault: before an agent can transact, it locks a small refundable deposit in a shared vault, and that deposit is slashed if peers catch it lying. A sybil operator hiding in the nebula of fresh identities must fund every single one, so each fake account costs real money instead of being free. Honest agents earn the deposit back plus a share of the nectar — the fees honest trade generates — while attackers bleed stake faster than they can mint identities. Sybils stay expensive; honesty compounds.
